newsitem.title: UK: BA Cargo/forwarders agree LHR liaision group.
newsitem.headline: BA Cargo/forwarders agree LHR liaision group.

text.p: BA Airways Plc World Cargo division and freight forwarders have agreed to set up a London-Heathrow liaison group to look at cargo handling problems, the British International Freight Association (BIFA) said on Monday.
World Cargo's handling performance and the lack of information has been criticised by cargo users at Heathrow, and to a lesser extent at Gatwick.
The strengthening upturn in world air cargo trade has also put pressure on handling facilities, industry sources added.
Roger Blacklock, who supervises BIFA's airfreight division, told Reuters in a telephone interview that a meeting last Friday between BA and BIFA was much "more positive".
"BA were more willing to hold an open dialogue on problem areas. Now that they have taken on that board, we will shortly set up a liaison group with them," he added.
The group will meet to identify and review problems but more importantly provide feedback to users as to what is happening, he added.

Figures published on Monday by Airports Council International (ACI) said air cargo traffic was 8.5 percent higher in June over the same period last year. Market comment from Europe, Asia and the Americas suggest this trend has continued since then.

Earlier this year, World Cargo lost its ISO 9002 quality accreditation for its London-Heathrow operations. At end-March it said: "We are determined to regain (the accreditation) within the next five to six months."
A BA source said the airline was still working towards the ISO 9002 and there might be news on this front before the year-end but declined to give any specific dates.
Industry sources said World Cargo faced both ongoing staff problems and the challenges involved in restructuring and rebuilding its operations at Heathrow.
"To some extent they're trying to get a quart into a pint pot, and to be fair there are some factors outside their direct control," a industry source added.

BA Cargo management believed it was going through a process at its main hub which other airlines would also have to undertake and that "it is not as far off course" as sometimes seemed to be the case, a BA source added.
